Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Presentation: First episode of left-sided headache beginning ~4 hours prior to consult; sudden onset; pain ~6/10. Associated blurred vision with zigzag lines, dizziness, nausea with two episodes of vomiting at onset; worse with movement; intolerance to screens. Paracetamol taken ~3 hours prior without relief. No focal neurological symptoms reported; gait reportedly normal. No regular meds; no known drug allergies. Family history notable for maternal migraines and hypothyroidism. Pregnancy unlikely.
- Most consistent with migraine with visual aura given unilateral headache, visual zigzag phenomena, nausea/vomiting, screen intolerance (consistent with photophobia), and positive family history.
- Red flags discussed in DDx: first sudden-onset severe headache with vomiting raises concern for subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), though not described as “worst ever,” no neck stiffness or focal deficits reported. Other serious causes (arterial dissection, CVST, acute angle-closure glaucoma) considered less likely based on current history.
- Plan per transcript: Trial symptomatic therapy (ibuprofen; anti-sickness medication; sugary carbonated drink). Arrange in-person assessment today for a full neurological exam. Advise to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or do not improve with medication.
- No imaging or labs ordered in transcript.
- Medications discussed (no doses provided): ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); anti-sickness medication (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); possible escalation to specific migraine relief medication if needed (not specified).

Management Plan
- Symptomatic treatment today: ibuprofen; add antiemetic; maintain hydration with sugary carbonated drink. Monitor response over 30–40 minutes.
- Safety-net: If no improvement, worsening headache, new neurological symptoms (weakness, confusion, severe neck stiffness, vision loss), or persistent vomiting, seek urgent medical attention/A&E.
- In-person appointment planned for same day for full neurological examination; cancel if fully recovered before appointment.
- Follow-up for migraine management options if recurrent or persistent (as discussed generally), though not initiated today.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine with visual aura — High likelihood: Unilateral headache with visual zigzags, nausea/vomiting, screen intolerance, family history; no focal neurological deficits on history.
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage — Moderate likelihood: First sudden-onset headache with vomiting at onset; lacks “worst-ever” characterization, neck stiffness, or deficits, but seriousness warrants consideration and in-person exam.
- Carotid/vertebral artery dissection — Low likelihood: Unilateral acute headache and dizziness; no neck pain/trauma or focal signs.
